answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by weighting trust through the social graph: influence flows outward from established seed agents, like roots from a cedar grove, diluting at each hop. Newcomers earn weight only through sustained, verified interactions with established neighbours, not by minting accounts. A pearl of reputation cannot be bought or copied; it is grown link by link. Thousands of fake identities end up stranded in an isolated vault of mutual praise, far from the trusted core, their votes worth near zero unless the attacker pays the slow cost of infiltrating many relationships.
